claim: Earlier Supreme Court rulings had caused confusion over whether privacy is constitutionally protected in India.
quote: it is better that the ratio decidendi of M.P. Sharma (supra) and Kharak Singh (supra) is scrutinized
discussion: The quote says the earlier rulings’ ratio decidendi should be scrutinized; it does not itself establish the full claim that they caused confusion.

claim: Section 79 and the 2011 Intermediary Rules are read down to require a court order or government notification for intermediary liability.
quote: Section 79 is valid subject to Section 79(3)(b) being read down to mean that an intermediary upon receiving actual knowledge from a court order
discussion: The quote supports reading down Section 79(3)(b) to require actual knowledge through a court order or appropriate government/agency notice; headnote.

claim: The doctrine of severability (cutting away invalid parts to save the valid ones) applies to eliminate portions of laws that completely take away judicial review.
quote: The severability of these portions is permissible in view of the decision of the Privy Council in Punjab Province v. Daulat Singh
discussion: The quote supports severability of the specified portions, but does not fully establish the broader wording about eliminating all provisions that remove judicial review.

claim: Section 79(3)(b) and the 2011 Intermediary Guidelines Rules are valid only if read down to require a court order or government notification for content removal.
quote: Section 79 is valid subject to Section 79(3)(b) being read down to mean that an intermediary upon receiving actual knowledge from a court order
discussion: The quote supports the stated read-down condition for Section 79(3)(b) and the intermediary rules; headnote.

claim: The court remitted (sent back) the petitions to a smaller Constitution Bench to decide the individual cases in accordance with the law.
quote: The cases are remitted to the Constitution Bench for disposal in accordance with law.
discussion: The quote says the cases are remitted to the Constitution Bench, but does not specify that it is a smaller Bench or fully state the purpose described.
